title: What If You Weighed 10x Less?
script: What if you weighed ten times less? Same muscles, a tenth of the weight. You jump for a frisbee and float over everyone. A kid's balloon slips away, so you leap up, grab the string, and the park cheers. Even an astronaut on the Moon weighs more than you. But then the wind starts winning. Grip comes from weight. Less weight, less grip, but wind shoves as hard as ever. So you live by one rule: one hand always holds something. Until you walk a windy cliff path with your little brother Sam and your best friend Mia, and the edge crumbles. Now both hang off the rocks. Let go of the railing, and the wind throws you off. Your free hand can pull up only one. Five. Four. Three. Sam is eight and screaming your name. Mia never once let you fall. Sam, or Mia? Who do you grab?

hud.label: REAL SCIENCE
hud.text: Less weight = less grip. Wind pushes just as hard.
